evidence.title: Historical mission context
evidence.establishes: Nothing on its own: it sets our predicted local sunset after each CLPS landing beside the end of the mission its operator reported.
can_tell: Whether our predicted sunset comes before or after a reported end, when the operator says the lander ran into the night (Blue Ghost Mission 1).
That the Sun was still up when IM-1 and IM-2 ended, so their ends had other causes.
cannot_tell: The hour of sunset: reported ends are announcements, two of them without a published hour.
Whether a battery would last a night, or anything about a lander's power system.
How often the forecast is right: one lander that ran to sunset is one case, not a sample.
limitations: Mission end times are reported events, not observed sunsets.
They are not battery-survival validation: a lander's end depends on its attitude, power system, temperatures and operations.
Blue Ghost's site is far from the pole and uses a flat horizon, which puts our sunset about 2.5 hours after the one Firefly reported.
evidence.command: cd pipeline && uv run python -m lunar_pipeline.cli validate

rows.name: IM-1 Odysseus landing site (Malapert A)
rows.mission_end_source: Intuitive Machines, IM-1 mission update 29 Feb 2024: final transmission as the lunar night began (hour not published; 00:00 UTC used)
rows.mission_note: Odysseus tipped onto its side at touchdown, with its panels tilted away from the low Sun; power ran out about three days before the predicted sunset.

rows.name: IM-2 Athena landing site (Mons Mouton)
rows.mission_end_source: Intuitive Machines / NASA release 7 Mar 2025: mission concluded, batteries depleted (hour not published; 12:00 UTC used)
rows.mission_note: Athena came to rest on its side in a crater with the Sun barely above the hills; its batteries drained within a day, with about twelve days of daylight left.

rows.name: Blue Ghost Mission 1 landing site (Mare Crisium)
rows.mission_end_source: Firefly Aerospace, Blue Ghost Mission 1 update 16 Mar 2025: mission concluded at 23:25 UTC, about 5 h after lunar sunset
rows.mission_note: Blue Ghost worked through the whole lunar day on the flat plain of Mare Crisium and fell silent about 5 hours after the sunset it saw. Our sunset, worked out for a flat horizon, comes about 2.5 hours after the one it saw, so its last signal came 2.4 hours after ours.
